title: Rabbi Elazar Chisma
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: (A Tanna of the Mishnah.) Why he was called Chisma is related in Vayikra Rabbah 23:4: once this Rabbi Elazar came to a certain place, and they asked him to lead the Shema and pass before the ark, and he could not. They said to him, “If so, why do they call you Rabbi?” He was ashamed, and went to Rabbi Akiva, who taught him. When he came a second time to that place and they asked him to lead the Shema, he did so. They said, “Rabbi Elazar has become strong (itchasem),” and they called him Rabbi Elazar Chisma. Hyman therefore considers it clear that where in some places he is called Rabbi Elazar ben Chisma, it is a scribal error.

He was Rabbi Yehoshua’s student, as stated explicitly in Chagigah 3a: an incident in which Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka and Rabbi Elazar Chisma went to greet Rabbi Yehoshua in Peki’in … they said to him, “We are your students, and from your water we drink,” and they told him what Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah had expounded. Likewise we find in Tosefta Zavim, chapter 4: “Three things Rabbi Elazar Chisma declares impure in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua.” Likewise in the Mekhilta, Beshalach, beginning of parashah deAmalek: “Rabbi Yehoshua and Rabbi Elazar ben Chisma say” (Hyman proposes Rabbi Elazar Chisma). Both were in Rabban Gamliel’s academy and studied Torah in poverty, and Rabban Gamliel did not know of this; through Rabbi Yehoshua their teacher they were raised up, as related in Horayot 10b [supplied locator; see note]: Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Yehoshua were traveling on a ship … Rabban Gamliel said to Rabbi Yehoshua, “You have so much wisdom, and you go up on a ship?” He said to him: “Rather than wondering at me, wonder at two students you have on land, Rabbi Elazar Chisma and Rabbi Yochanan ben Gudgeda (Hyman proposes Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri, as in Sifrei Devarim 16), who know how to calculate how many drops there are in the sea, and they have no bread to eat and no garment to wear.” He set his mind to seat them at the head. When he went up [to land], he sent for them, and they did not come; he sent again, and they came. He said to them: “Do you think I am giving you authority? I am giving you servitude.”

He is mentioned in the Mishnah, Avot, end of chapter 3, where he said: “Bird-offerings and the openings [calculations of menstrual periods] — these are the essentials of the halakhot; astronomy and gematriot (the science of calculation) are the after-courses of wisdom” (and this is as Rabbi Yehoshua testified of him). He is likewise mentioned in Terumot 3:5 together with Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov (and likewise we find in Pesachim 32a that they disagree face to face, for both were Rabbi Akiva’s students); in Bava Metzia 7:5 he holds that a worker should not eat more than his wage (and there it is ben Chisma, but in the Jerusalem Talmud, Maaserot, end of chapter 2, the reading is Rabbi Elazar Chisma); and in Negaim 7:3 and 13:3 he disagrees with Rabbi Yehudah, and Mikvaot 8:3.

In baraitot he is mentioned in Gittin 62a: “Rabbi Yose ben HaMeshullam testified in the name of Rabbi Yochanan his brother, who said in the name of Rabbi Elazar ben Chisma.” In Tosefta Zavim 1:2, Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Yannai in his name; and there, Temurah, chapter 4, Rabbi Chananyah ben Antigenos in his name (but Hyman prefers the reading of Mishnah Temurah 6:5, where Rabbi Elazar Chisma is not mentioned, for according to the chronology Rabbi Chananyah ben Antigenos was older than Rabbi Elazar Chisma). He is likewise mentioned in the Mekhilta, Beshalach, Massekhta deVayassa.

Eliezer ben Yaakov is fully written in ToratEmetMishnahTerumot3:5 and DavidsonPesachim32a, distinct from ElazarChisma. פתחי נדה are menstrual opening/calculation laws rather than an unqualified ordinary onset. The consulted Vayikra Rabbah 23:4 contains the liturgical-learning story; Terumot 3:5 and Pesachim 32a distinguish Elazar Chisma from Eliezer ben Yaakov. The full consulted ship and appointment sequence begins in Horayot 10a and ends with the servitude declaration at 10b; Hyman’s supplied 10b is retained. The direct text names Yochanan ben Gudgeda, while Hyman proposes ben Nuri from Sifrei. His clear deletion of ben from Chisma, the Sifrei/Mekhilta/Tosefta edition claims and the chronological preference for the Mishnah Temurah reading remain his arguments, without automatic name harmonization.
